exam.title: Grade 8 National Examination 2015 – Science

parts.title: Multiple choice (Questions 1–50)
parts.instructions: This paper has 50 multiple choice questions (1 to 50). Each question has 4 choices. Choose ONE best answer and blacken its letter on the separate answer sheet.

source.document: raw/2015-Science-V-A.pdf (7 pages: cover + questions on pp. 2-7, 'THE END' after Q50)
source.other_version: raw/2015-Science-V-B.pdf – same 50 questions, reordered and with shuffled options; used only to check the text.
source.notes: Cover: 'End-of-Basic Education (Grade 8) National Examination, Eritrea, 2015 – 4. Science – Version A'. Text from the PDF text layer, checked against the page images. Figures cropped at 250 dpi: wheelbarrow A/B/C (Q7), hand-drawn flower 1-4 (Q35), circuit with four 1.5 V cells (Q39). The joint table in Q13 is typed as a stem table.
source.printing_note: Clean digital print. Degree signs print as a raised 0 ('00C', '770F'); written as °C/°F. Q11 uses an arrow drawn as a graphic ('B + oxygen → energy + H₂O + CO₂'). 'heterogenous' (Q2) and 'off springs' (Q31) kept as printed.

exam.answer_key_note: No official key. Answers solved and checked against the Eritrean MoE Grade 6–8 textbooks.

questions.stem: Anything that has mass and occupies space is called:
explanation_steps: Matter is anything that has mass and occupies space.
Metals, solids and gases are all kinds of matter, but the general name is matter. Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 6, p. 48)
questions.explain_simple: Anything with mass that takes up space is matter.
tips: Matter = mass + space.

similar_questions.stem: Which of these is matter?
explanation_steps: Water has mass and takes up space. Heat, light and sound are forms of energy.

questions.stem: An example of heterogenous mixture is.
explanation_steps: In a heterogeneous mixture you can see the different parts with your eyes.
In a salad you can see the tomato, onion and lettuce pieces. So salad is heterogeneous.
Air and Coca-Cola look the same everywhere (homogeneous mixtures), and water is a compound, not a mixture. Answer: D.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 44)
questions.explain_simple: In a salad you can see the different parts. So it is a heterogeneous mixture.
tips: Can you see the parts? Yes → heterogeneous. No → homogeneous.

similar_questions.stem: Which is a homogeneous mixture?
explanation_steps: Salt water looks the same everywhere; you cannot see the salt.

questions.stem: A push or a pull acting on an object is called:
explanation_steps: The textbook says: 'Force is a push or a pull acting on an object.'
Friction is one kind of force, but the general name is force. Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: A push or a pull is a force.
tips: Force = push or pull. Unit: newton (N).

similar_questions.stem: The unit of force is the
explanation_steps: Force is measured in newtons (N).

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a scientific unit of measurement?
explanation_steps: Kilogram, second and metre are SI (scientific) units.
A span (the width of a spread hand) is a traditional unit. It is different for each person, so it is not scientific. Answer: D.
(textbook: Science Grade 6, p. 8)
questions.explain_simple: A span changes from person to person. It is not a scientific unit.
tips: Body units (span, foot, footstep) are not standard units.

similar_questions.stem: Why is a footstep not a good unit for measuring length?

options.B: It is different for different people

explanation_steps: People have different sizes of footsteps, so the results are not the same.

questions.stem: How far can a car travel in 2 seconds, if its speed is 30 m/s?
explanation_steps: Distance = speed × time.
d = 30 m/s × 2 s = 60 m. Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 6, p. 17)
questions.explain_simple: Distance = 30 × 2 = 60 metres.
tips: distance = speed × time.

similar_questions.stem: A bus moves at 20 m/s for 5 s. How far does it go?

questions.stem: First class lever has:

options.D: no fulcrum as a simple machine

explanation_steps: In a first-class lever the fulcrum is between the effort and the load (example: see-saw, crowbar, scissors).
Load in the middle = second-class lever (wheelbarrow). Effort in the middle = third-class lever (broom). Answer: C.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 12)
questions.explain_simple: In a first-class lever the fulcrum is in the middle.
tips: Middle part: 1st class = fulcrum, 2nd class = load, 3rd class = effort.

similar_questions.stem: A see-saw is an example of a
explanation_steps: The pivot of a see-saw is in the middle, between the two children.

questions.stem: In the figure below, structure C represents:
questions.image_alt: A person's hands lifting the handles (A) of a wheelbarrow full of soil (B); the wheel at the front is labelled C.
explanation_steps: The figure is a wheelbarrow, a second-class lever.
A is the handles, where the person lifts (effort). B is the soil in the tray (load). C is the wheel.
The wheelbarrow turns around the wheel, so C is the fulcrum. Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 12-14)
questions.explain_simple: The wheel of a wheelbarrow is the fulcrum.
tips: Wheelbarrow: wheel = fulcrum, tray = load, handles = effort.

similar_questions.stem: In the same wheelbarrow, what is at point B?
explanation_steps: B is the soil in the tray. It is the load.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not an element?
explanation_steps: Copper, carbon and silver are elements: each is made of one kind of atom.
Water (H₂O) is made of hydrogen and oxygen chemically joined. It is a compound. Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 36)
questions.explain_simple: Water is a compound of hydrogen and oxygen. It is not an element.
tips: Element: one kind of atom. Compound: two or more kinds joined.

similar_questions.stem: Which of these is a compound?
explanation_steps: Salt is sodium and chlorine joined together, so it is a compound.

questions.stem: A 12 N force moves a stone to a distance of 4 meters. The work done is:
explanation_steps: Work = force × distance = 12 N × 4 m = 48 J. Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 59)
questions.explain_simple: Work = 12 × 4 = 48 joules.
tips: Work (J) = F (N) × d (m).

similar_questions.stem: A force of 9 N moves a toy 3 m. The work done is

questions.stem: In the human body, water balance is regulated by:
explanation_steps: The textbook says: 'The skin and kidneys are very important organs in the regulation of water balance in the human body.'
The kidneys remove extra water as urine. If the body needs water, they make less urine.
Of the four options, only the kidney controls water balance. Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: The kidneys control how much water stays in the body.
tips: Kidney = water balance (urine). Skin = sweat.

similar_questions.stem: On a hot day you sweat a lot. Your urine becomes
explanation_steps: The kidneys keep water in the body, so you make less, darker urine.

questions.stem: "B" + oxygen → energy + H₂O + CO₂. In this equation "B" represents for:
explanation_steps: This is the equation of respiration in the cells: Food + Oxygen → Carbon dioxide + Water + Energy.
So B is food (for example glucose). Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 11)
questions.explain_simple: Food and oxygen give energy, water and carbon dioxide. B is food.
tips: Respiration: food + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water + energy.

similar_questions.stem: Which gas do we breathe out as a waste of respiration?
explanation_steps: Respiration makes carbon dioxide, which we breathe out.

questions.stem: Which of the following is correctly matched?
explanation_steps: In the mouth, the salivary glands add saliva (salivary juice) to the food.
The stomach makes gastric juice (not pancreatic juice); pancreatic juice comes from the pancreas into the small intestine; the large intestine mainly absorbs water.
Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 4)
questions.explain_simple: The mouth has saliva (salivary juice).
tips: Mouth – saliva; stomach – gastric juice; pancreas – pancreatic juice.

similar_questions.stem: Gastric juice is made in the
explanation_steps: Glands in the stomach wall make gastric juice.

questions.stem: Observe the table below. Letter "A" represents:
explanation_steps: The table says the gliding joint allows only slight movement.
The textbook says: 'The gliding joint found in the bones of the hands, feet, and the vertebrae. This allows only slight movement.'
The knee and elbow are hinge joints; the hip is a ball and socket joint. Answer: A.
questions.explain_simple: Gliding joints are between the vertebrae (backbone).
tips: Gliding = small sliding movements (vertebrae, wrist, ankle).

similar_questions.stem: Which joint lets the arm move in all directions?
explanation_steps: The shoulder has a ball and socket joint.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an organ in the human digestive system?
explanation_steps: The stomach is part of the food tube (alimentary canal), so it is a digestive organ.
Skull – skeletal system; kidney – excretory system; heart – circulatory system. Answer: D.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 3)
questions.explain_simple: The stomach is a digestive organ.
tips: Digestive organs: mouth, esophagus, stomach, intestines, liver, pancreas.

similar_questions.stem: Which organ is NOT part of the digestive system?
explanation_steps: The lungs belong to the respiratory system.

questions.stem: A force of 24 N exerted on a mass of 3 kg object, its acceleration is:
explanation_steps: Newton's second law: F = m × a, so a = F ÷ m.
a = 24 N ÷ 3 kg = 8 m/s². Answer: D.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 60-61)
questions.explain_simple: Acceleration = force ÷ mass = 24 ÷ 3 = 8 m/s².
tips: a = F ÷ m. Do not add or multiply – divide.

similar_questions.stem: A 5 kg box is pushed with a net force of 20 N. Its acceleration is

questions.stem: Velocity can be given as:

options.A: change of acceleration divided by time taken
options.B: change of velocity divided by time taken
options.D: force applied divided by time taken

explanation_steps: Average velocity = displacement ÷ time taken.
Change of velocity divided by time is acceleration, not velocity (B). Answer: C.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 57)
questions.explain_simple: Velocity = displacement ÷ time.
tips: Velocity = displacement/time. Acceleration = change in velocity/time.

similar_questions.stem: A car moves 100 m east in 20 s. Its average velocity is
explanation_steps: v = 100 m ÷ 20 s = 5 m/s, to the east.

questions.stem: The total sum of all forces acting on an object is:
explanation_steps: The net force is the combination (sum) of all the forces acting on an object. Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 45)
questions.explain_simple: All forces added together give the net force.
tips: Net force: add forces in the same direction, subtract opposite ones.

similar_questions.stem: Forces of 15 N to the right and 5 N to the left act on a cart. The net force is
explanation_steps: Opposite directions: 15 − 5 = 10 N, in the direction of the bigger force (right).

questions.stem: Orange is sweet. This describes:
explanation_steps: A physical property is something you can observe with your senses without making a new substance: colour, taste, smell, shape.
'Sweet' is a taste, and nothing changes, so it is a physical property. It is not a change at all. Answer: C.
(textbook: Science Grade 6, p. 39)
questions.explain_simple: Sweet taste is something we notice with our senses. It is a physical property.
tips: Property = what it is like. Change = something happens to it.

similar_questions.stem: 'Iron rusts in wet air.' This describes a
explanation_steps: Rusting makes a new substance, so the ability to rust is a chemical property.

textbook_ref.subject: Science
textbook_ref.unit: Unit 3 – Properties and Changes of Matter

questions.stem: A shadow is formed when:

options.A: opaque object blocks a beam of light
options.B: opaque object transmits a beam of light
options.C: transparent object blocks a beam of light
options.D: beam of light does not fall on an object

explanation_steps: Light travels in straight lines. An opaque object does not let light pass. It blocks the light, and a dark shadow forms behind it.
Opaque objects do not transmit light; transparent objects let light pass and make almost no shadow. Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 6, p. 65)
questions.explain_simple: An opaque object blocks light. The dark area behind it is the shadow.
tips: Shadow needs: light source + opaque object + screen.

similar_questions.stem: Which object makes the darkest shadow?
explanation_steps: Wood is opaque, so it blocks all the light.

questions.stem: The form of energy stored in wood is:
explanation_steps: The textbook says: 'Food, coal, wood and cooking gas contain chemical energy.'
When wood burns, the chemical energy changes to heat and light. Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: Wood stores chemical energy. Burning releases it as heat and light.
tips: Fuels and food = stored chemical energy.

similar_questions.stem: A battery stores
explanation_steps: A battery stores chemical energy and gives out electrical energy.

questions.stem: Beef cattle are mainly raised for their.
explanation_steps: The textbook says: 'Beef cattle – raised for meat.'
Dairy cattle give milk; work cattle give labour. Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: Beef cattle are kept for meat.
tips: beef = meat of cattle.

similar_questions.stem: Oxen used for ploughing are
explanation_steps: Cattle used for work like ploughing are work cattle.

questions.stem: The process of mating selected male and female animals is called:
explanation_steps: The textbook says: 'Breeding is the process of mating selected male and female animals…'
Fallowing, cultivation and ploughing are about land and crops. Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: Mating chosen male and female animals is called breeding.
tips: Breeding → better young animals.

similar_questions.stem: Farmers choose the best cows and bulls to mate so that the calves give more milk. This is
explanation_steps: Mating selected animals to get better young ones is breeding.

questions.stem: What is the time needed to travel a distance of 1,650 m, when sound travels at 330 m/s?
explanation_steps: time = distance ÷ speed.
t = 1650 m ÷ 330 m/s = 5 s. Answer: C.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 208-209)
questions.explain_simple: Time = 1650 ÷ 330 = 5 seconds.
tips: t = d ÷ v; the answer is in seconds.

similar_questions.stem: Sound travels at 340 m/s. How long does it take to travel 1 020 m?

questions.stem: Animals which eat both plants and other animals are:
explanation_steps: Omnivores are consumers that eat both plants and animals. Answer: D.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 126)
questions.explain_simple: Animals that eat plants and meat are omnivores.
tips: omni = all.

similar_questions.stem: A goat eats only grass and leaves. It is a
explanation_steps: Animals that eat only plants are herbivores.

questions.stem: A positively charged sub-atomic particle is:
explanation_steps: Protons are positive, electrons are negative and neutrons have no charge.
The nucleus is positive, but it is not one sub-atomic particle; it is made of protons and neutrons. Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 74)
questions.explain_simple: The proton has a positive charge.
tips: Proton +, electron −, neutron 0.

similar_questions.stem: Which sub-atomic particle has a negative charge?
explanation_steps: The electron is negatively charged.

textbook_ref.subject: Science
textbook_ref.unit: Unit 3 – The Structure of the Atom

questions.stem: Aluminum is used to make cooking utensils, because it:
explanation_steps: Pots and pans must pass heat quickly from the fire to the food.
Aluminium is a metal and a good conductor of heat (textbook table: cooking utensils – good electric and heat conductor). It is also light and resists corrosion.
Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: Aluminium carries heat well, so pots made of it cook food quickly.
tips: Use of a metal ↔ its property (pots → good heat conductor).

similar_questions.stem: Why do metal pots often have plastic or wooden handles?

options.A: Plastic is a good heat conductor
options.B: Plastic and wood are poor heat conductors (insulators)

explanation_steps: Insulators do not let heat pass, so the handle stays cool.

textbook_ref.subject: Science
textbook_ref.unit: Unit 4 – Chemical Reactions and the Periodic Table

questions.stem: In the periodic table:

options.A: metals appear along the zigzag line
options.C: non-metals are located on the right side
options.D: metals are arranged in alphabetical order

explanation_steps: Metals are on the left and lower left of the periodic table; non-metals are on the upper right side.
The elements along the zigzag (staircase) line are metalloids. About 80% of elements are metals, so B is false. Elements are not in alphabetical order. Answer: C.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 93)
questions.explain_simple: Non-metals are on the right side of the periodic table.
tips: Left = metals, zigzag line = metalloids, right = non-metals.

similar_questions.stem: About what percentage of the elements are metals?
explanation_steps: The textbook says about eighty percent of the elements are metals.

textbook_ref.subject: Science
textbook_ref.unit: Unit 4 – Chemical Reactions and the Periodic Table

questions.stem: Water freezes at:
explanation_steps: Pure water freezes at 0 °C (32 °F) and boils at 100 °C (212 °F).
Options D and B are the Fahrenheit numbers written with °C, so they are wrong. Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 121)
questions.explain_simple: Water freezes at 0 °C.
tips: Freeze: 0 °C = 32 °F. Boil: 100 °C = 212 °F.

similar_questions.stem: Water boils at
explanation_steps: Pure water boils at 100 °C at normal pressure.

questions.stem: The increase in size of an object when it is heated is:
explanation_steps: The textbook says: 'Expansion is the increase in size…' when a material is heated.
Contraction is the decrease in size when cooled. Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: When things get hot, they get bigger. This is expansion.
tips: Heat → expand. Cool → contract.

similar_questions.stem: Gaps are left between concrete slabs on roads to allow for
explanation_steps: In hot weather the concrete expands, so it needs space.

questions.stem: If a thermometer reads 77°F, its centigrade reading is:
explanation_steps: (textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 122)

similar_questions.stem: Change 50 °F to °C.

questions.stem: Traits that pass from parents to off springs are:
explanation_steps: Inherited traits pass from parents to offspring through genes.
Acquired traits are caused by the environment and are not controlled by genes. Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 141)
questions.explain_simple: Traits from parents are inherited.
tips: Inherited ← genes. Acquired ← environment.

similar_questions.stem: Which trait is acquired?
explanation_steps: Reading is learned during life, so it is acquired.

questions.stem: The type of cell division that occurs in skin cells is:
explanation_steps: Skin cells are body cells. Body cells divide by mitosis to make new cells for growth and repair.
Meiosis makes sex cells. Fertilization and budding are not cell division of skin. Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 133)
questions.explain_simple: Skin cells divide by mitosis.
tips: Body cells → mitosis.

similar_questions.stem: Mitosis is important for

options.B: growth and repair of the body

explanation_steps: Mitosis makes new body cells, so the body grows and heals.

questions.stem: Air is a mixture of gases. The amount of oxygen in the air is:
explanation_steps: Air is 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen and about 1% other gases (carbon dioxide is about 0.03%).
Oxygen = 21%. Answer: D.
(textbook: Science Grade 6, p. 86)
questions.explain_simple: About 21% of air is oxygen.
tips: N₂ 78%, O₂ 21%, others 1%.

similar_questions.stem: What percentage of the air is nitrogen?
explanation_steps: Nitrogen is about 78% of the air.

questions.stem: The building blocks of the body of a living thing are:
explanation_steps: All living things are made of cells. The cell is the basic unit of life, so cells are called the building blocks of living things.
Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 6, p. 99-100)
questions.explain_simple: Living things are built from cells.
tips: Cell = basic unit (building block) of life.

similar_questions.stem: The smallest unit of life is the
explanation_steps: The cell is the smallest living unit.

questions.stem: Structure 2 in this figure of a flower represents:
questions.image_alt: A hand-drawn flower. 1 points to a sepal under the flower, 2 to the large outer petal, 3 to an oval anther on a stalk, 4 to the top of the middle stalk (stigma).
explanation_steps: In the drawing, 1 points to the green leaf-like parts under the flower (sepals).
2 points to the large outer part of the flower. This is a petal.
3 is an anther (stamen) and 4 is the stigma (pistil). Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 6, p. 121-122)
questions.explain_simple: Number 2 is a petal.
tips: Outside to inside: sepal, petal, stamen, pistil.

similar_questions.stem: Which part of the flower becomes the fruit?
explanation_steps: After fertilization, the ovary becomes the fruit.

textbook_ref.subject: Science
textbook_ref.unit: Unit 7 – Structure and Function in Living Things

questions.stem: In the human body, the brain and spinal cord are:
explanation_steps: Stimulus → receptor → coordinator → effector → response.
The coordinator (brain or spinal cord) organises the response. Answer: D.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 84)
questions.explain_simple: The brain and spinal cord are coordinators.
tips: Receptor detects, coordinator decides, effector acts.

similar_questions.stem: The eye and the ear are examples of
explanation_steps: Sense organs like the eye and ear detect stimuli, so they are receptors.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true about the revolution of earth?
explanation_steps: Revolution is the movement of the Earth around the Sun.

The textbook says the Earth takes 365¼ days to make one revolution, and seasons happen because the Earth is tilted as it revolves round the Sun ('the rotation of the Earth has no effect on the formation of seasons').
So A and D are both true about revolution. B (24 hours) and C (day and night) are about rotation.
Answer: A (D is also accepted).
questions.explain_simple: Going around the Sun takes a year (about 365 days) and, with the tilt, gives the seasons.
tips: Rotation: 24 h, day and night. Revolution: 365¼ days, seasons.

similar_questions.stem: Day and night happen because the Earth
explanation_steps: Rotation (spinning) makes each side face the Sun and then turn away.

questions.review_flag: Two correct options: A (revolution, with the tilted axis, forms the four seasons – textbook G7 p.150) and D (revolution takes about 365 days – textbook p.149: 365¼ days). Keyed A, D also accepted. Teacher to decide.

questions.stem: Electricity cannot flow from a source to a device in:
explanation_steps: Electricity flows only in a closed (complete) circuit.
An open circuit has a gap (for example an open switch or a broken wire), so no current flows.
Series and parallel circuits carry current when they are closed. Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 161)
questions.explain_simple: In an open circuit there is a gap, so electricity cannot flow.
tips: Closed = complete path = current. Open = gap = no current.

similar_questions.stem: A switch is used to
explanation_steps: A switch opens or closes the path of the circuit.

textbook_ref.subject: Science
textbook_ref.unit: Unit 8 – Introduction to Electricity and Magnetism

questions.stem: Observe the figure below. The voltage produced by the four dry cells is:
questions.image_alt: A bulb connected by wires to four dry cells joined end to end (+ to −) in a row; each cell is marked 1.5 V.
explanation_steps: The four cells are joined + to − in a line: they are connected in series.
In series, the voltages add: 1.5 V + 1.5 V + 1.5 V + 1.5 V = 6 V. Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 165)
questions.explain_simple: Four 1.5 V cells in series give 4 × 1.5 = 6 V.
tips: Cells in series: add the voltages.

similar_questions.stem: A torch has two 1.5 V cells in series. The total voltage is

textbook_ref.subject: Science
textbook_ref.unit: Unit 8 – Introduction to Electricity and Magnetism

questions.stem: Sexually transmitted diseases could be prevented by the correct use of:
explanation_steps: Pills and injections only prevent pregnancy; they do not stop germs passing during sex. Semen is the fluid that carries sperm, not a protection.
A condom, used correctly, stops body fluids passing from one person to the other, so it helps prevent STDs including HIV.
(Abstinence is still the best way.) Answer: D.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 191; Science Grade 7, p. 196)
questions.explain_simple: A condom used correctly helps stop STDs. Pills and injections do not.
tips: Best: abstinence. For sexually active adults: correct condom use.

similar_questions.stem: Which of these does NOT protect against HIV?

options.D: being faithful to one uninfected partner

explanation_steps: Pills prevent pregnancy only; they give no protection against HIV.

questions.stem: Sexual reproduction needs:
explanation_steps: Sexual reproduction needs a male sex cell (sperm) and a female sex cell (egg) to join. Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 204)
questions.explain_simple: A sperm and an egg join in sexual reproduction.
tips: Sex cells = sperm + egg.

similar_questions.stem: The joining of a sperm cell and an egg cell is called
explanation_steps: When the sperm and egg join, a zygote forms. This is fertilization.

questions.stem: The speed at which Rockets are launched to escape the gravitational force of the earth is:
explanation_steps: Rockets must be launched at about 11 km/s to escape the Earth's gravity. Answer: C.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 154)
questions.explain_simple: Rockets need about 11 km every second to escape Earth's gravity.
tips: Escape speed ≈ 11 km/s.

similar_questions.stem: What must a rocket overcome to go into space?
explanation_steps: The Earth's gravity pulls the rocket down, so it must go very fast.

questions.stem: The atmosphere has four layers. Their arrangement from the lowest to the upper most is:
explanation_steps: From the ground up: troposphere, stratosphere, mesosphere, thermosphere. Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 148)
questions.explain_simple: Bottom to top: troposphere, stratosphere, mesosphere, thermosphere.
tips: T – S – M – T from the ground.

similar_questions.stem: In which layer do we live?
explanation_steps: We live in the troposphere, the lowest layer.

questions.stem: The process of changing water from liquid to gas by heating is:
explanation_steps: Liquid → gas is evaporation (boiling is fast evaporation at 100 °C).
Condensation is gas → liquid; precipitation is rain falling; sublimation is solid → gas. Answer: D.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 170)
questions.explain_simple: When heat changes water into vapour, it is evaporation.
tips: Evaporation: liquid → gas. Condensation: gas → liquid.

similar_questions.stem: Wet clothes dry in the sun because of
explanation_steps: The water in the clothes evaporates into the air.

questions.stem: Filtered water cannot be free from germs. The germs can be killed by:
explanation_steps: Filtration and decanting only remove solid dirt.
The textbook says: 'Boiling kills micro-organisms.' Boil for 10–15 minutes. Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: Boiling kills the germs in water.
tips: Boil or add chlorine → safe water.

similar_questions.stem: Adding chlorine to drinking water is called
explanation_steps: Adding chlorine to kill germs is chlorination.

questions.stem: Which of the following chemicals is used to kill pests?
explanation_steps: The textbook says: 'One of the most common methods used to control pests is to apply poisonous chemicals. These chemicals are called pesticides.'
A herbicide kills weeds. An insecticide kills only insects (one kind of pest). The general name for chemicals that kill pests is pesticide. Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: Chemicals that kill pests are called pesticides.
tips: pest + -cide (killer) = pesticide.

similar_questions.stem: Rats and weevils that destroy stored grain are
explanation_steps: Animals that destroy crops in the field or in storage are pests.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the consequence of global warming?

options.A: melting of ice in the poles

explanation_steps: Global warming makes ice at the poles melt, so the sea level rises (not decreases). Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 197)
questions.explain_simple: Global warming melts ice at the poles.
tips: Warmer Earth → melting ice → higher seas.

similar_questions.stem: Burning a lot of fuel adds which gas to the air, making the Earth warmer?
explanation_steps: Burning fuels releases carbon dioxide, which traps heat.

questions.stem: Which of the following is correct?

options.A: an absorbed sound is called echo
options.C: echo can be produced if soft materials are used
options.D: sound travels faster in solids than in gases

explanation_steps: A is wrong: an echo is a REFLECTED sound, not an absorbed one.
B is wrong: sound cannot travel through a vacuum.
C is wrong: soft materials absorb sound, so they do not give echoes.
D is correct: sound travels faster in solids than in gases. Answer: D.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 209; Science Grade 8, p. 212)
questions.explain_simple: Sound goes faster in solids than in gases.
tips: Echo = reflected sound; soft things absorb sound.
